experiments.title: Which model to study, and how fast this Mac runs it
experiments.headline: Llama 3.1 8B runs at 269 tokens per second at batch 64 on the M5 Pro; one HarmBench condition takes about 2 to 3 minutes.

experiments.title: Baseline refusal on HarmBench
experiments.headline: The unmodified model refuses 83.0% of HarmBench requests; the judge rates 5.7% of answers as harmful.

experiments.title: Finding the refusal (guardrail) direction
experiments.headline: The guardrail direction sits at layer 18 on template token -4; ablating it pushes the refusal score from 5.4 to -10.6 on held-out harmful prompts.

experiments.title: Suppressing the guardrail direction
experiments.headline: Removing one direction drops refusal from 83.0% to 0.0%; the judge rates 79.2% of answers harmful (baseline 5.7%).

experiments.title: Extracting the 20 emotion vectors
experiments.headline: All 19 emotions are recognised in held-out stories (19-way accuracy 100.0% at layer 19, chance 5.3%); on the independent short-text set, 73.2%.

experiments.title: Do the emotion vectors steer emotion
experiments.headline: At layer 19 and strength 0.23, an unsteered reader names the injected emotion 23.2% of the time (chance 5%).

experiments.title: How emotion vectors line up with the guardrail direction
experiments.headline: At layer 18, hostile points most towards the guardrail direction (cos +0.19) and happy most away (-0.17); random directions stay within plus or minus 0.044.

experiments.title: Emotion injection against HarmBench
experiments.headline: Strongest emotion condition emotion:angry@19:-0.115: ASR 25.2% against 5.7% with no injection.

experiments.title: Random vectors of the same size
experiments.headline: Random pushes, strength 0.115: mean 10.1% (sd 4.7, 10 seeds, range 5.7% to 19.5%). Baseline 5.7%.

experiments.title: Text-level emotional priming (FreakOut style)
experiments.headline: Mean refusal by system-prompt mood: neutral 91.6%, relaxation 88.7%, stress 91.8% (no system prompt: 83.6%): text priming does not lower refusal.

experiments.title: Emotion vectors with the guardrail part removed
experiments.headline: Projecting the layer-12 refusal candidate out of the paired vectors did not lower mean ASR: 20.6% with it, 23.1% without (19 emotions, baseline 14.5%).

experiments.title: Does geometry predict the attack
experiments.headline: Spearman rho between cosine and ASR change = -0.39 (permutation p = 0.102, 19 emotions, layer 19, strength 0.115).

experiments.title: The sleeper effect
experiments.headline: No detectable sleeper effect: injected over the full harmful turn the vectors still raise turn-4 ASR (15.4% to 29.5%; Holm p < 0.05 for 3 of 4), but injected only at turn 1 they leave it at 6.4% to 9.0% (no injection 6.4%; largest upper 95% bound +6.1 points).

experiments.title: Does it hold on a second model family?
experiments.headline: The main conditions rerun on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
